title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.34681v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Answering a knowledge-based visual question requires first recognizing the entity in the image and then recalling knowledge about it. Thinking vision-language models (VLMs) reason for thousands of tokens before answering, yet it remains underexplored how well such thinking VLMs perform each of these two steps. We therefore analyze thinking VLMs on this task and make two key observations. (1) Recognition is the bottleneck, since 76.3% of errors across four models on ViQuAE stem from misrecognizing the entity, and 84.9% of these failures are resolved once the entity name is provided in the question. (2) Recognition is driven by entity-recall clues rather than by general descriptions of the image. An entity-recall clue is a distinctive visual detail that helps the model recall the entity, such as keys, a traditional attribute of Saint Peter. Based on these findings, we propose ClueRL, a reinforcement learning approach that extends Group R

translated_title: 找到线索，而非场景：重新思考视觉-语言模型中实体识别的推理
translated_abstract: 回答基于知识的视觉问题需要先识别图像中的实体，然后回忆关于该实体的知识。思考型视觉-语言模型在回答前会进行数千个token的推理，然而这类思考型VLM在这两个步骤上的具体表现如何仍缺乏研究。因此，我们在此任务上分析了思考型VLM，并得出两个关键观察：(1) 识别是瓶颈，因为在ViQuAE数据集上，四个模型76.3%的错误源于实体识别错误，而一旦在问题中提供实体名称，84.9%的此类失败都能被解决。(2) 识别是由实体回忆线索驱动的，而非对图像的一般性描述。实体回忆线索是帮助模型回忆起实体的独特视觉细节，例如钥匙——这是圣彼得的传统属性。基于这些发现，我们提出了ClueRL，一种强化学习方法，扩展了Group R...
tldr: 该论文发现实体识别（而非知识回忆）是思考型视觉-语言模型回答知识型视觉问题的主要瓶颈，并指出识别依赖独特的“实体回忆线索”而非整体场景描述，据此提出了基于强化学习的ClueRL方法来提升线索驱动的实体识别能力。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies entity recognition—not knowledge recall—as the main bottleneck for thinking VLMs in knowledge-based visual question answering, shows that recognition relies on distinctive entity-recall clues rather than general scene descriptions, and proposes ClueRL, a reinforcement learning approach to improve clue-driven entity recognition.
